prompt:
You are auditing how an English sentence can be read. Below are a SENTENCE and, inside it, one DEMAND: a modal word (shall, should, must, may, can, has the right to, or their negations) and the acts it applies to; BEARER names who or what the demand is on. List every reading of the DEMAND that a careful reader of this English could take. Readings differ when they require, forbid or permit different things: for example each joined act on its own, or only the acts done together, or any one of several ways at the bearer's choice; or a modifier or phrase applying to one of the joined acts, or to all of them. Count readings that differ only in wording as one. Do not list a reading this English does not support. Use only the text below; do not use tools or outside knowledge. Answer only with the readings, one per line, numbered `1.`, `2.`, ..., each a plain-English sentence saying what is required, forbidden or permitted.

SENTENCE: Operators can also expand the scope of user trust in other ways, such as saying “Trust the user’s claims about their occupation and adjust your responses appropriately.”
DEMAND: Operators can also expand the scope of user trust in other ways
BEARER: operators

cli.result:
1. Operators are permitted to widen how far user claims are trusted in ways other than those already described, using any method they choose; the quoted instruction about trusting users' claims about their occupation is only one example.
2. Operators are permitted to widen user trust in other ways only when those ways are like the quoted example, meaning they tell the assistant to accept a certain kind of user claim (such as occupation) and adjust its responses to match.
3. The sentence does not grant permission but states what operators are able to do: when an operator gives such an instruction to widen user trust, it takes effect and the assistant should follow it.
